title: Ubiquitin receptor–mediated, ubiquitin-independent targeted protein degradation via 26S proteasomes

figures.label: Fig. 1.
figures.caption: The Protea-Tac system enables engineered degradation of target proteins through direct proteasome engagement.(A) Schematic illustration of TPD by Protea-Tac. (B) A549 cells were transfected with c-Fos and PSMD4-scFv(c-Fos) or LacZV5 for 64 hours; WCLs were analyzed by SDS-PAGE/IB and total protein staining. Total plasmid DNA amounts and volumes remained constant across all experimental conditions. Left: Representative IBs from three independent experiments. Right: c-Fos quantification. Protein quantification was normalized to total protein unless indicated otherwise. N = 3, means ± SD, ****P < 0.0001; one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc test. (C) c-Fos mRNA was measured by qRT-PCR and normalized to GAPDH. N = 4, means ± SD, n.s., not significant; one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc test. (D) Cycloheximide (CHX) chase after transfection as in (B), with c-Fos normalized to 0 hours in each group. MCL1 served as a physiological proteasome substrate. N = 3, means ± SD, *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01; two-way ANOVA with Sidak’s post hoc test. (E to G) scFv(c-Fos)-ADRM1 was evaluated as in (B) to (D). (H) Proteasome subunit–based chimeras were transiently expressed in A549 cells and analyzed by IB. (I) Hexahistidine-biotin (HB)–tagged PSMD4-scFv(c-Fos) was purified by streptavidin affinity purification and analyzed by native PAGE, in-gel suc-LLVY-AMC hydrolysis, and IB; 0.02% SDS activated 20S proteasomes. (J) Endogenous c-Fos and cyclin D1 proteins were compared in MCF7 cells stably expressing EGFP or scFv(c-Fos)-ADRM1. (K) c-Fos and cyclin D1 mRNAs were measured by qRT-PCR and normalized to GAPDH. N = 3, means ± SD, ***P < 0.001, n.s.; two-tailed Student’s t test. (L and M) Transient scFv(c-Fos)-ADRM1 expression in MCF7 cells was assessed by IB and qRT-PCR. N = 3, means ± SD, ****P < 0.0001, n.s.; two-tailed Student’s t test. See fig. S1.

figures.label: Fig. 2.
figures.caption: Protea-Tac degraders require both UbR and tAb modules.(A and B) A549 cells were transfected with c-Fos and PSMD4- or ADRM1-based components expressed either separately or as UbR–scFv(c-Fos) fusions; WCLs harvested at 64 hours were analyzed by SDS-PAGE/IB and total protein staining. Protein quantification was normalized to total protein unless indicated otherwise. (C) Bicistronic and tricistronic constructs encoding scFv(c-Fos)-ADRM1 without or with a T2A sequence at the tAb-UbR junction, followed by P2A-mCherry, were expressed in HEK293T cells stably expressing EGFP–c-Fos and analyzed by flow cytometry. Histograms show EGFP–c-Fos fluorescence in mCherry-positive cells. (D) EGFP mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) in mCherry-positive cells. N = 3, means ± SD, ****P < 0.0001; two-tailed Student’s t test. (E) HEK293 cells stably expressing HB-tagged PSMB2 were transfected as in (A) with untagged PSMD4-scFv(c-Fos) and PSMD4H to assess competitive proteasome incorporation and target degradation. Affinity-purified proteasomes and WCLs were analyzed by denaturing SDS-PAGE/IB for c-Fos and proteasome subunits. (F) PSMD4-scFv(c-Fos) was coexpressed with noncognate ADRM1 and assessed for c-Fos degradation. (G to I) Lower-affinity T206K and higher-affinity T206E scFv(c-Fos) variants were evaluated in ADRM1-based degraders. (G) Representative IBs from three independent experiments. (H) c-Fos protein quantification. N = 3, means ± SD, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001; one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple comparison test. (I) c-Fos mRNA measured by qRT-PCR and normalized to GAPDH. N = 4, means ± SD, n.s.; one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc test. See fig. S2.

figures.label: Fig. 3.
figures.caption: The Protea-Tac system enables Ub-independent and proteasome-mediated TPD.(A) scFv(c-Fos)-ADRM1–mediated c-Fos degradation was examined in the presence of dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), the proteasome inhibitor MG132 (10 μM), the vacuolar type H+-ATPase inhibitor bafilomycin A1 (BafA1; 200 nM), or the E1 Ub-activating enzyme inhibitor MLN7243 (1 μM) for 6 hours. (B) The steady-state levels of c-Fos detected across conditions in (A) were quantified and normalized to total protein. Each bar indicates the means ± SD (N = 3). ****P < 0.0001 (one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey’s multiple comparison test). (C and D) As in (A) and (B), except that VHH(GFP)-ADRM1 was used as a degrader and GFP-ODC was a neo-substrate. (E) Chase experiments were performed to track the degradation kinetics of EGFP-tagged version of c-Fos (EGFP–c-Fos) in the presence of DMSO or MLN7243. (F) Quantification of EGFP–c-Fos band intensities in (E), normalized to those of total protein and to the values at 0 hours post–CHX treatment (set as 100%), under DMSO (top) or MLN7243 (bottom) treatment conditions. Average percentages of remaining EGFP–c-Fos (means ± SD) from three independent experiments (N = 3); *P < 0.05, ****P < 0.0001 (two-way ANOVA followed by Sidak’s post hoc test). (G and H) Chase experiments and quantification using EGFP–c-Fos as in (E) and (F) except that they were performed in the presence of either DMSO or MG132. Data represent the means ± SD from three independent experiments (N = 3). ***P < 0.001 (two-way ANOVA followed by Sidak’s post hoc test). n.s., not significant. See fig. S3.

figures.label: Fig. 4.
figures.caption: Protea-Tac–mediated degradation is highly selective and modular via UbR and tAb exchanges.(A) Schematic of Protea-Tac modularity through interchangeable tAb units. (B to I) A549 cells transiently expressing FlagTDP43, HAtau, GFPODC, or endogenous BRD4 were treated with cognate Protea-Tac degraders or controls and analyzed by SDS-PAGE/IB, total protein staining, and qRT-PCR. Protein quantification was normalized to total protein unless indicated otherwise; qRT-PCR values were normalized to GAPDH. (B and C) PSMD4-scFv(Flag) degraded FlagTDP43 without reducing TDP43 mRNA. Protein: N = 3, means ± SD, ****P < 0.0001; mRNA: N = 4, n.s.; two-tailed Student’s t test. (D and E) scFv(HA)-ADRM1 degraded HAtau without reducing tau mRNA. Protein: N = 3, means ± SD, ****P < 0.0001; mRNA: N = 4, n.s.; two-tailed Student’s t test. (F and G) PSMD4-VHH(GFP) degraded GFP-tagged ODC without reducing GFP mRNA. Protein: N = 3, means ± SD, ***P < 0.001; mRNA: N = 4, n.s.; two-tailed Student’s t test. (H and I) Lentiviral ADRM1-scFv(BRD4) reduced endogenous BRD4 protein but not BRD4 mRNA. Protein and mRNA: N = 3, means ± SD, ***P < 0.001 or ns; two-tailed Student’s t test. (J and K) Mismatched c-Fos–targeting Protea-Tac did not degrade FlagTDP43 or HAtau. (L) TMT-LC-MS/MS global proteome profiling compared A549 stably overexpressing c-Fos cells transfected by scFv(c-Fos)-ADRM1 or ADRM1 plus scFv(c-Fos) controls. Among 6295 quantified proteins, 16 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were identified using |log2FC| > 0.263 and adjusted P value < 0.05. (M) Volcano plot of differentially expressed proteins, with c-Fos and ADRM1 highlighted in red. (N) Native PAGE analysis of 26S proteasomes by in-gel suc-LLVY-AMC hydrolysis and IB; 0.02% SDS activated 20S proteasomes. (O) Endogenous protein levels in HCT116_EGFP and HCT116_scFv(c-Fos)-ADRM1 stable cells were analyzed by IB. See fig. S4.

figures.label: Fig. 5.
figures.caption: Protea-Tac–induced c-Fos degradation leads to antitumor efficacy in vivo.(A) MCF7 cells stably expressing EGFP or scFv(c-Fos)-ADRM1 were subcutaneously inoculated into 6-week-old male NSG mice, and tumor volumes were measured twice weekly for ∼5 weeks. Data are means ± SEM, N = 8 per group, ****P < 0.0001; Mann-Whitney U test. Insets show tumors harvested on day 32. (B) Tumors harvested on day 50 from HCT116_EGFP or HCT116_scFv(c-Fos)-ADRM1 xenografts established as in (A). (C) Body weight changes during the HCT116 xenograft experiment. (D) IB analysis of tumor lysates. (E) Quantification of c-Fos and cyclin D1 proteins, normalized to total protein signals. Data are means ± SD, N = 8, ****P < 0.0001; two-tailed Student’s t test. (F) qRT-PCR analysis of c-Fos and cyclin D1 mRNAs, normalized to GAPDH. Data are means ± SEM, N = 8, ***P < 0.001, n.s.; two-tailed Student’s t test. (G) Cell cycle distribution of MCF7 stable cells used for xenograft assays, analyzed by DAPI staining and flow cytometry. N = 3, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001, n.s.; two-way ANOVA with Sidak’s post hoc test. (H) MCF7-xenografted NSG mice were intratumorally injected three times per week with PBS, AAV2-EGFP, or AAV2-scFv(c-Fos)-ADRM1, and tumor growth was measured three times per week for 50 days. Data are means ± SEM, N = 6 per group, ****P < 0.0001; two-way ANOVA with Sidak’s post hoc test. (I) Body weight changes during the AAV2-delivery experiment. (J) IB analysis of tumor lysates. (K) c-Fos protein quantification. Data are means ± SD, N = 6, ***P < 0.001, n.s.; one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc test. (L) qRT-PCR analysis of c-Fos and cyclin D1 mRNAs. Data are means ± SEM, N = 5, **P < 0.01; one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc test. See figs. S5 and S6.

figures.label: Fig. 6.
figures.caption: mRNA-LNP–mediated Protea-Tac expression inhibits tumor growth in vivo.(A) A549-xenografted 6-week-old female BALB/cAnN-Foxn1nu/Crl mice received subcutaneous (sc) injections of PBS or LNP formulations containing mRNA encoding EGFP, scFv(c-Fos), or PSMD4-scFv(c-Fos). Representative image of tumors harvested is shown. (B) Tumor volumes were measured twice a week for 21 days. LNP formulations were administered subcutaneously every 5 days for a total of three doses. Each formulation contained 40 μg of mRNA per dose. Data are presented as means ± SEM (N = 6 per group); two-way ANOVA followed by Sidak’s post hoc test (****P < 0.0001). (C) IB analysis of whole-tumor lysates with indicated antibodies. (D) Quantification of c-Fos (left) and cyclin D1 (right) protein levels, normalized to total protein signals. Bars represent the means ± SD (N = 3). n.s., not significant, *P < 0.05 (one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc test). (E) As in (D), but mRNA levels of c-Fos and cyclin D1 were determined using qRT-PCR and normalized to GAPDH. Bars represent the means ± SEM (N = 3). n.s., not significant, **P < 0.01 (one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc test).
